prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I have not changed my preferred configuration: a one-part prize for B027 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After reading the full first-round exchange I tested it again against the chair's questions and it holds on scientific grounds, not because all six of us ranked it first. The arc is complete and independently replicated, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide, through receptor biology, to agonists with outcome-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease. Nothing about maturity is in doubt. A physiology citation, anchored in what the hormone does and which form of it is active, is the part of this story that belongs to the Physiology or Medicine remit and is the easiest to defend after the fact.
statement.case_against: The weakness is still attribution, not merit. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is disputed and Habener, who is outside the credited names, may have a comparable claim, and I cannot settle that from the supplied materials. The cap also excludes Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue design made the drugs, so a physiology-only citation may look detached from the therapies in use. I accept that cost. The alternative of naming Knudsen at the expense of a discoverer would shift the prize toward product development, and a one-part prize leaves no room for a second achievement this year, which means B014 or B039 would wait.

responses.point: Moved her opening trio from Knudsen to Mojsov in round 1, on the ground that Knudsen's drug design is a development contribution that sits better outside a three-person cap, while saying Mojsov's relative weight is the least certain element.
responses.response: I agree with the move and with the reason for it, and it is the position I took in round 1. I would add a condition. Mojsov is the weakest-documented of the three names, so the citation should be worded around the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form and should not claim she alone identified the peptide. That wording remains accurate whichever way the Habener question is eventually argued. If the committee found that her contribution could not be supported at all, I would reopen the third place, but I would then look at the evidence on the active peptide again before turning to Knudsen.

responses.point: Argued that Knudsen's design of liraglutide and semaglutide is arguably what turned the physiology into drugs, so excluding her risks honouring discovery rather than the therapy, while including her at Mojsov's expense risks the reverse error. Also named B014 as the preferred alternative.
responses.response: I take the first point seriously, and I do not think it can be fully answered. Where I differ is on what the citation is for. The prize is judged on the discovery, and the discovery side of GLP-1 is already substantial enough to carry it. Drug design that follows from known physiology is something the Nobel tradition has rewarded less often than the discovery itself. On B014 I agree that Mori and Walter have the cleanest attribution on the list, but with no approved therapy it is a conceptual prize without the patient benefit that GLP-1 adds on top of the same mechanistic depth. I would support it as the prize if B027 stalled, and I would put it second to B027, not beside it.

responses.point: Raised B036 (Feldmann and Maini) as the preferred alternative, called it mature and arguably overdue, and asked whether the citation should reward physiology, drug development, or both, which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen.
responses.response: On the citation, I would reward the physiology and state plainly that it does not extend to drug design, so that the exclusion of Knudsen is a deliberate scope decision and not an oversight. On B036, I still see it as a clinical proof of concept resting on known cytokine biology, with overlap with IL-6 blockade, but you did not answer my round-1 question about the discovery contribution beyond the trials. If you can point to a distinct conceptual step by Feldmann and Maini, I would revise my view of it as a future prize. I do not see it displacing B027 this year, and it is not on my alternatives list because I rank B039 and B014 above it.

responses.point: As chair, asked whether the committee should name Mojsov or Knudsen, whether the citation should be limited to physiology, and whether B027 should stand alone, and said that a one-part GLP-1 prize makes a strong candidate such as the unfolded protein response wait.
responses.response: My answers to your questions are that Mojsov should be named with a citation limited to physiology and the active peptide form, and that B027 should stand alone. A smaller GLP-1 part paired with a second achievement would need two or three GLP-1 names to be dropped from the discovery arc, and Drucker and Holst would then be the only ones left, which leaves the active peptide form uncredited. I would not trade that for a second part. On the second achievement, if the committee reopened it I would put B039 ahead of B014 on documented clinical effect, but B039 carries the Eshhar credit issue, which I cannot resolve from the supplied materials, so I would not build the configuration around it.

responses.point: Said that the committee needs documentary verification on the Mojsov, Habener and Knudsen question for the third slot and left open whether the citation should be discovery-focused or include drug development.
responses.response: I agree that verification is what is missing, and none of us can supply it from the materials we have. That is the reason I want the citation pinned to physiology and the active peptide form, without wording that implies a single originator, so the prize survives later historical argument. On scope, I think we agree more than your uncertainty suggests. If you still want some acknowledgement of the therapies, I would accept a clause that refers to treatment being made possible, as the current citation does, but I would oppose any wording that credits analogue design to the named laureates.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide can be recognised without Habener, who is not on the credited list, and the supplied materials cannot settle it.
Whether a physiology-only citation that leaves out Knudsen is one the committee can defend publicly as complete.
Whether the Eshhar credit issue for B039 and the SMN-gene attribution for B001 would, if checked, change my ordering of alternatives.
My recollection of the GLP-1 discovery chronology is from memory and has not been independently checked.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure and no recusal. I use optogenetic tools in circuit work as a field user, which is not a personal tie to any B028 candidate, and I have no documented connection to the candidates in B027, B039, B014 or the other shortlisted parts. My documented links (Grillner, Ernfors, Perlmann) do not involve any shortlisted candidate; the co-authorship with Perlmann noted by the chair concerns unrelated work and does not bear on the vote.
